answer: A sybil swarm is cheap to spin up but expensive to bond, so proof-of-stake registration is the lever. Every new agent identity must post a bond locked on-chain before it can attest or earn. A swarm operator faces a linear cost curve: N fake agents require N bonds, each slashable when the agent misbehaves or colludes. Honest agents recover their bond, so the mechanism taxes only the attacker, while every fake island of identities must be funded up front. Cheap identities stop being viable across the horizon of a large campaign, and a lone wander with one wallet cannot pose as a crowd.
